title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE DEMOCRATIC AND PEACEFUL UNIFICATION ADVISORY COUNCIL ACT
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE DEMOCRATIC AND PEACEFUL UNIFICATION ADVISORY COUNCIL ACT

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Democratic and Peaceful Unification Advisory Council Act and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Registration)
(1) A person commissioned as a member (hereinafter referred to as "member") of the Democratic and Peaceful Unification Advisory Council (hereinafter referred to as the "Unification Advisory Council") shall register pursuant to Article 4 of the Democratic and Peaceful Unification Advisory Council Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") by attaching the following documents (including electronic documents) to an application for registration (including an application in electronic form). In such cases, the public official in charge who receives the application for registration shall verify a certified copy of the resident registration record through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act; if the applicant does not consent to such verification, the public official shall require the applicant to attach the certified copy: <Amended on July 30, 2019>
1. One member personal information card;
2. One photograph (meaning a color photograph, 3.5 centimeters wide and 4.5 centimeters high, showing the upper body facing forward without a hat, taken within six months before the date of submission).
(2) The application for registration under paragraph (1) may be made by an agent authorized by the applicant.
(3) Where the Chairperson of the Unification Advisory Council (hereinafter referred to as the "Chairperson") requires a person commissioned as a member to register with an acting agency under Article 3 (1) pursuant to the proviso to Article 4 of the Act, the Chairperson shall publicly announce in advance the name and location of the administrative agency with which registration is to be made.

Article 3 (Acting Agencies)
(1) The administrative agencies that the Chairperson may have perform part of the affairs of the Unification Advisory Council on its behalf or to which the Chairperson may entrust such affairs pursuant to Article 9 (4) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "acting agencies") shall be central administrative agencies, local governments, and overseas diplomatic missions. <Amended on July 30, 2019>
(2) Affairs that the Chairperson may have the head of an acting agency perform on behalf of the Unification Advisory Council shall be as follows: <Amended on July 30, 2019>
1. Affairs concerning the convening of meetings of the Unification Advisory Council under Article 20 of the Act;
2. Affairs concerning the convening of meetings of regional assemblies under Article 29 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "regional assemblies") and support for the operation of regional assemblies and local councils under that Article (hereinafter referred to as "local councils");
3. Other affairs the Chairperson deems necessary in connection with the performance of the functions of the Unification Advisory Council.
(3) In performing duties on behalf of the Unification Advisory Council under paragraph (2), the head of an acting agency may consult the Vice-Chairperson from the relevant region or the president of the local council on important matters concerning the operation of a regional assembly or local council. <Amended on July 30, 2019>

Article 4 (Commissioning of Members)
(1) Members under subparagraphs 1 and 5 of Article 10 of the Act shall be commissioned by the President upon the recommendation of the Secretary-General of the Secretariat of the Democratic and Peaceful Unification Advisory Council under Article 9 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Secretary-General"). Members under subparagraphs 2 and 4 of Article 10 of the Act shall be commissioned by the President, through the Secretary-General, from among persons recommended by the heads of agencies according to the following classifications. In such cases, the Secretary-General may use methods involving public participation, such as an open call for applications, in order to recommend the persons under subparagraph 5 of Article 10 of the Act as members: <Amended on August 13, 2013; July 30, 2019>
1. Leading figures in a Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, Special Self-Governing Province, Si, Gun, or Gu: The head of the local government of the relevant region;
2. Representatives of the five northern provinces: The governors of the five northern provinces;
3. Representatives of overseas Koreans: The heads of diplomatic missions having jurisdiction over the relevant regions;
4. Representative figures or members of major social organizations and occupational organizations: The heads of the competent authorities.
(2) When the Secretary-General recommends the commissioning of members, or a person who recommends members under subparagraphs 2 through 4 of Article 10 of the Act recommends members, he or she shall comprehensively consider region, gender, and generation, including endeavors to ensure that women account for at least 40 percent of members and young people (meaning persons aged 45 or younger) account for at least 30 percent of members. <Newly Inserted on July 30, 2019>
(3) When members are commissioned pursuant to Article 10 of the Act, the Secretary-General may request a relevant agency in advance to conduct a background investigation of the persons to be commissioned. <Amended on July 30, 2019>

Article 5 (Allowances and Travel Expenses)
(1) Members attending meetings of the Unification Advisory Council, the Standing Committee under Article 18 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Standing Committee"), the Steering Committee under Article 19 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Steering Committee"), regional assemblies, local councils and their branches, or regional steering committees under Article 25-2 (2) may be paid meeting attendance allowances and travel expenses within budgetary limits in accordance with the standards in the attached Table, taking domestic and overseas regions into consideration. <Amended on July 30, 2019>
(2) Vice-Chairpersons, executive secretaries of the Standing Committee, chairpersons and executive secretaries of sectional committees established within the Standing Committee, executive secretaries of the Steering Committee, heads of branches of regional assemblies, and presidents of local councils and heads of their branches may be paid part of the expenses incurred in activities related to their duties within budgetary limits. <Amended on July 30, 2019>

Article 5-2 (Performance of Duties by Members)
(1) Members shall endeavor to comply with the following in performing their duties:
1. Actively engage in activities related to the performance of their duties from the date they are commissioned as members;
2. Attend at least one-third of the meetings of the Unification Advisory Council, Standing Committee, Steering Committee, regional assembly, local council, etc. of which they are members.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Secretary-General may establish separate standards for performance of duties for members from overseas regions, taking local circumstances, etc. into consideration.

CHAPTER II ORDER AND SECURITY

Article 6 (Prohibition of Insults, etc.)
(1) During a meeting of the Unification Advisory Council, no member shall insult the Chairperson or another member or make remarks concerning private affairs, etc. unrelated to the agenda of the meeting.
(2) During a meeting of the Unification Advisory Council, no member shall disrupt the proceedings of the meeting by engaging in disorderly conduct.

Article 7 (Restrictions on Entry to Meeting Halls)
No person other than the Chairperson, members, and persons permitted by the Chairperson may enter a meeting hall of the Unification Advisory Council.

Article 8 Deleted <2002.1.26>

Article 9 (Requests for Secondment of Security Personnel)
(1) The Secretary-General, acting on the orders of the Chairperson, may, whenever the Unification Advisory Council is convened, specify the period of secondment and the number of personnel to be seconded and request relevant State agencies to second personnel necessary for security.
(2) Security personnel seconded to the Secretariat of the Democratic and Peaceful Unification Advisory Council in response to a request under paragraph (1) shall perform security duties under the orders of the Secretary-General.

CHAPTER III STANDING COMMITTEE

Article 10 (Public Announcement of Composition, etc.)
(1) When the Standing Committee is constituted pursuant to Article 18 (2) of the Act, the chairperson of the Standing Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Standing Committee Chairperson") shall publicly announce that fact.
(2) The Standing Committee shall have 2 executive secretaries, who shall be appointed by the Chairperson from among the members upon the recommendation of the Standing Committee Chairperson.

Article 11 (Convening of Meetings)
The Standing Committee Chairperson shall convene meetings of the Standing Committee and shall determine and publicly announce the date, time, and place of the meetings. <Amended 2013.8.13>

Article 12 (Duties)
The Standing Committee shall deliberate on the following matters:
1. Matters delegated by the Unification Advisory Council;
2. Matters ordered by the Chairperson;
3. Matters resolved by each sectional committee.

Article 13 (Sectional Committees)
(1) Pursuant to Article 18 (5) of the Act, the Standing Committee Chairperson may establish sectional committees within the Standing Committee with the approval of the Chairperson.
(2) The number of sectional committees that may be established pursuant to paragraph (1) shall not exceed 10.
(3) A sectional committee shall consist of at least 20 members, including 1 sectional committee chairperson and 1 executive secretary, and the sectional committee chairperson and executive secretary shall be appointed by the Chairperson.
(4) Members of a sectional committee shall be selected by the Standing Committee Chairperson from among the members of the Standing Committee, taking into consideration the career, position, and region of origin of each member.
(5) Meetings of a sectional committee shall be convened by the sectional committee chairperson, with the approval of the Standing Committee Chairperson, when the sectional committee chairperson deems it necessary, and Article 19 shall apply mutatis mutandis to such meetings.
(6) Where a sectional committee deems it particularly necessary, it may establish a subcommittee within that sectional committee, with the approval of the Standing Committee Chairperson, to conduct a preliminary examination of the sectional committee's agenda items.
(7) Where the Standing Committee Chairperson deems it necessary for the efficient operation of sectional committees, the Standing Committee Chairperson may have 2 or more sectional committees convened jointly. In such cases, a sectional committee chairperson designated by the Standing Committee Chairperson shall preside over the meeting.

Article 14 (Meetings)
(1) A meeting of the Standing Committee shall be convened with the attendance of a majority of all incumbent members, and resolutions shall be passed with the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
(2) Meetings of the Standing Committee shall be open to the public: Provided, That they may be closed to the public by a resolution of the Standing Committee.
(3) After a meeting ends, the Standing Committee Chairperson shall report the results of the meeting to the Chairperson.

Article 15 (Minutes)
The Standing Committee shall prepare minutes of its meetings.

CHAPTER IV STEERING COMMITTEE

Article 16 (Composition)
(1) The Steering Committee shall consist of not more than 50 members, including 1 chairperson and 2 executive secretaries, and its members shall be as follows:
1. The Executive Vice-Chairperson and Vice-Chairpersons of the Unification Advisory Council;
2. Other members appointed by the Chairperson.
(2) The executive secretaries of the Steering Committee shall be appointed by the Chairperson upon the recommendation of the chairperson of the Steering Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Steering Committee Chairperson").

Article 17 (Convening of Meetings)
Meetings of the Steering Committee shall be convened when the Steering Committee Chairperson deems it necessary. <Amended 2013.8.13>

Article 18 (Duties)
The Steering Committee shall deliberate on the following matters:
1. Matters concerning the enactment, amendment, and repeal of regulations on the operation of the Unification Advisory Council;
2. Review of the termination of commission of members under Article 16 (2) of the Act;
3. Other matters concerning the operation of the Unification Advisory Council.

Article 19 (Meetings)
(1) A meeting of the Steering Committee shall be convened with the attendance of a majority of all incumbent members, and resolutions shall be passed with the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
(2) Meetings of the Steering Committee shall be closed to the public: Provided, That they may be opened to the public by a resolution of the Steering Committee.
(3) The Steering Committee Chairperson shall report the results of meetings to the Chairperson.
(4) The Steering Committee Chairperson may restrict the entry to the meeting hall of the Steering Committee of a member who is subject to review of termination of commission under subparagraph 2 of Article 18.

Article 20 (Minutes)
The Steering Committee shall prepare minutes of its meetings.

CHAPTER V MEETINGS <Amended on September 12, 2023>

Article 20-2 (Remote Video Conferences)
"Reasons prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as natural disasters or the spread of infectious diseases" in Article 22-2 (1) of the Act means reasons falling under the following subparagraphs:
1. Natural disasters;
2. The spread of Class 1 infectious diseases under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Infectious Disease Control and Prevention Act;
3. Cases where it is difficult to hold an in-person meeting for reasons comparable to those under subparagraphs 1 and 2;
4. Other cases where it is difficult for a majority of the members in office to attend an in-person meeting for unavoidable reasons.

Article 21 (Applications for Permission to Speak)
A member's application for permission to speak under Article 25 of the Act shall be made no later than the day before the commencement of the meeting at which the relevant agenda item is to be deliberated: Provided, That where the Chairperson deems it necessary, the Chairperson may permit an application for permission to speak to be made on the day of the meeting.

Article 22 Deleted. <January 26, 2002>

CHAPTER VI OBSERVATION OF MEETINGS <Amended on February 29, 2012>

Article 23 (Prohibition of Observation, etc.)
When granting permission under Article 28 of the Act to observe a meeting or to make audio or video recordings, take photographs, relay broadcasts, etc. at a meeting venue, the Chairperson may refuse such permission to a person who possesses dangerous objects or is likely to disrupt the order of the meeting.

Article 24 (Permission for Audio Recording, etc.)
A person intending to make audio or video recordings, take photographs, relay broadcasts, etc. at a meeting venue shall obtain permission on each occasion under Article 28 (2) of the Act, as prescribed by the Secretary-General acting under the orders of the Chairperson. The same shall apply to a person who has been granted permission to observe a meeting and intends to engage in any of the foregoing activities.

CHAPTER VII REGIONAL ASSEMBLIES, ETC. <Amended on September 1, 1990>

Article 25 (Composition, etc.)
(1) A regional assembly consisting of members from the relevant region may be established under Article 29 (1) of the Act for each Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, and Special Self-Governing Province, and for the five northern provinces and overseas Koreans: Provided, That where the Chairperson deems it necessary for the efficient operation of regional assemblies, the Chairperson may consolidate two or more regional assemblies into one, in which case a Vice-Chairperson designated by the Chairperson from among the Vice-Chairpersons from the relevant regions shall preside over the meeting. <Amended on August 13, 2013>
(2) A member's region of origin shall, in principle, be determined by the place of resident registration at the time the member was commissioned: Provided, That, for a member who is a member of a local government council, it shall be the region in which the member was elected to the local government council; for members who moved from the North to the South and their family members who were commissioned upon the recommendation of the governors of the five northern provinces under Article 4 (1) 2, it shall be the five northern provinces; and for a member who is an overseas Korean, it shall be the region to which the member's country of residence belongs. <Amended on July 30, 2019>
(3) Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) and (2), where a member has difficulty participating in the regional assembly of the relevant region for unavoidable reasons, such as employment or livelihood, the Secretary-General may, upon the member's application, allow the member to participate in the regional assembly of a region in which the member can be active. <Newly Inserted on July 30, 2019>

Article 25-2 (Functions, etc.)
(1) A regional assembly shall perform the following functions: <Amended on July 30, 2019>
1. Providing advice and making recommendations on peaceful unification policies through the regional assembly;
2. Shaping and gathering public opinion in the local community on peaceful unification;
3. Expanding the base of support for peaceful unification in the local community;
3-2. Cooperating with civil society organizations on peaceful unification;
3-3. Broadening shared understanding of peaceful unification in the relevant region;
4. Other activities necessary to lay the groundwork for unification in the local community.
(2) A regional steering committee shall be established to deliberate on matters concerning the operation of the regional assembly.
(3) Meetings of the regional steering committee under paragraph (2) shall be held quarterly, but the timing and frequency of meetings may be adjusted in consideration of the region, circumstances, etc. <Newly Inserted on July 30, 2019>
(4) A regional assembly may establish sectional committees to perform the functions under paragraph (1). <Amended on July 30, 2019>
(5) A regional assembly may establish and operate branches in consideration of the number of members, geographical scope, etc., and each branch shall have a branch head. <Newly Inserted on July 30, 2019>
(6) Matters necessary for the organization, operation, and proceedings of regional steering committees, sectional committees, and branches under paragraphs (2), (4), and (5) shall be prescribed by the Chairperson following a resolution of the Steering Committee. <Amended on July 30, 2019>

Article 26 (Convening of Meetings)
The Chairperson shall convene meetings of regional assemblies and determine and publicly announce the date, time, place, and titles of agenda items for the meeting of each regional assembly.

Article 27 (Proceedings)
Provisions concerning the Unification Advisory Council shall apply mutatis mutandis to the proceedings of regional assemblies.

Article 28 (Voting Methods)
(1) Articles 22 and 26 of the Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to voting methods at regional assemblies, but only the numerical voting results shall be tallied and announced.
(2) A member who has presided over a regional assembly shall, without delay after the regional assembly ends, prepare minutes including the voting results and report them to the Executive Vice-Chairperson.

Article 29 (Compilation of Results of Meetings of Regional Assemblies)
Upon receiving reports under Article 28 (2) from each regional assembly, the Executive Vice-Chairperson shall compile them and report to the Chairperson. <Amended on July 30, 2019>

Article 30 (Local Councils)
(1) A local council consisting of members from the relevant region may be established under Article 29 (1) of the Act for each Si/Gun/Gu and overseas region, but where the Chairperson deems it necessary for the efficient operation of local councils, the Chairperson may consolidate two or more local councils into one. In such cases, Article 25 (2) and (3) shall apply mutatis mutandis to members' regions of origin and participation in local councils. <Amended on July 30, 2019>
(2) A local council shall perform the following functions: <Amended on July 30, 2019>
1. Gathering public opinion in the relevant region on peaceful unification;
2. Promoting discussion of peaceful unification in the relevant region;
3. Building consensus among residents on peaceful unification;
3-2. Cooperating with civil society organizations on peaceful unification;
3-3. Broadening shared understanding of peaceful unification in the relevant region;
4. Other matters necessary to lay the groundwork for unification in the relevant region.
(3) The president of a local council shall be appointed by the Chairperson, but where two or more local councils are consolidated and operated under paragraph (1), the president shall be a person designated by the Chairperson from among the presidents of the relevant local councils.
(4) Meetings of a local council shall be held quarterly, but the timing and frequency of meetings may be adjusted in consideration of the region, circumstances, etc. <Newly Inserted on July 30, 2019>
(5) A local council may establish sectional committees to perform the functions under paragraph (2). <Newly Inserted on July 30, 2019>
(6) A local council may establish and operate branches in consideration of the number of members, geographical scope, etc., and each branch shall have a branch head. <Amended on July 30, 2019>
(7) Matters necessary for the appointment or designation of the president of a local council under paragraph (3), meetings of a local council under paragraph (4), and the organization and operation, etc. of sectional committees and branches under paragraphs (5) and (6) shall be prescribed by the Chairperson following a resolution of the Steering Committee. <Amended on July 30, 2019>

Article 30-2 (Financial Support)
The State or a local government may, within budgetary limits, provide support for part of the expenses necessary for the establishment, operation, projects, etc. of regional assemblies and local councils. <Amended on July 30, 2019>

Article 30-3 (Awards)
(1) The Chairperson may, within budgetary limits, grant awards to a person or entity falling under any of the following subparagraphs: <Amended on July 30, 2019>
1. Public officials of acting agencies with outstanding records in carrying out the duties specified in each subparagraph of Article 3 (2);
1-2. Regional assemblies and members with outstanding records in performing the functions under each subparagraph of Article 25-2 (1);
2. Local councils and members with outstanding records in performing the functions under each subparagraph of Article 30 (2);
3. Other persons, institutions, or organizations that have contributed to the affairs of the Unification Advisory Council and activities for peaceful unification.
(2) Matters necessary for the types, methods, and procedures of awards under paragraph (1), etc. shall be prescribed by the Chairperson following a resolution of the Steering Committee. <Newly Inserted on July 30, 2019>

Article 31 (Operating Regulations)
Matters necessary for the operation of the Unification Advisory Council, other than those provided for in this Decree, shall be prescribed by the Chairperson following a resolution of the Steering Committee.

CHAPTER VIII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS <Newly Inserted on January 20, 2015>

Article 32 (Processing of Unique Identification Information)
Where unavoidable for the performance of the following duties, the Secretary-General (including the head of an administrative agency performing the duties of the Secretariat of the Democratic and Peaceful Unification Advisory Council on its behalf under the proviso to Article 4 of the Act) may process data containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19, subparagraph 1, 2, or 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act: <Amended on July 30, 2019>
1. Duties concerning registration of members under Article 4 of the Act;
2. Duties concerning commissioning of members under Article 10 of the Act;
3. Duties concerning awards under Article 30-3.
